newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Southcorp buys U.S. land for vineyard.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Southcorp buys U.S. land for vineyard.

text.p: Appliance manufacturer and winemaker Southcorp Holdings Ltd said on Friday it had bought a 250 hectare property in California to develop its first offshore vineyard.
Southcorp said the vineyard located near Paso Robles on the Californian central coast would be planted with 160 hectares of vines over the next three years with the first vintage expected in 2001.
Once completed, the total Californian development would represent an investment of about A$15 million, Southcorp said.
Planting would start in March 1998, initially with 80 hectares of Shiraz and Cabernet varieties.
The Paso Robles region was chosen because of its reputation as a premium red wine growing area in California and because it was similar to premium South Australian wine regions, it said.
Southcorp Holdings chief executive Graham Kraehe said the acquisition was part of the group's plan to target investments in growth businesses like wine.

"It is the latest element of the company's capital investment strategy to develop a truly global wine business and meet the growing worldwide demand for premium wine, particularly red varieties," Kraehe said.

Major winemakers such as the unlisted E & J Gallo, Robert Mondavi, Beringer and Sutter Home, as well as the French Rhone Valley producers of the premium Chateau de Beaucastel wines, had recently planted vineyards in the region,
Southcorp Wines is Australia's largest wine producer and the world's eighth largest producer.
It said it believed it was the world's largest vineyard holder with more than 6,000 hectares of vineyards in Australia.
Southcorp did not say how or where it would process the grapes grown at the vineyard.
A spokesman was not immediately available for comment.
